newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish retail climate improves in February.
newsitem.headline: Polish retail climate improves in February.

text.p: Poland's retail sector climate index improved in February on larger sales and an optimistic outlook for upcoming months, the Central Statistics Office (GUS) said in its first published retail sector report.
In its monthly survey GUS said the retail climate index rose to minus eight points in February from minus 13 in January with big firms registering the largest improvement.
The index, which is a percentage balance between positive and negative responses from polled companies, has been negative since September 1996 and hit a low in January.
In 1996 the retail index also hit a low in January before rising for the next several months.
GUS said that it would publish the retail index monthly, along with its industrial and construction sector climate.
Leading the sector were automotive retailers, whose index rose 30 points, and furniture, household equipment and electronics retailers, whose climate rose 25 points.
GUS also said that stock of inventories decreased slightly despite a rise in retail prices, which rose 2.9 percent in January and were expected to rise 1.7 percent in February.
